document: Protect Railway Workers Against Violent Crime, We call on the UK Government to review measures to protect railway workers from violent crime and strengthen them if necessary to ensure they are effective., Railway workers play a vital role in the UK. We feel they are committed to their roles, demonstrating dedication, resilience, and professionalism in providing vital services that connect communities. However, incidents of violent crime against them have been on the rise, particularly over the last three years with 3,330 recorded assaults on rail staff in the past financial year, a rise of almost 25% in a year and double the 1,681 attacks recorded on rail staff three years ago.

Increase speed limit from 70 mph to 90 mph on motorways., Please increase the speed limit on motorways., We think cars are more stable and can handle 90 mph on the motorways. We think it’s unnecessary to go at 70 mph when the roads are empty and delay the journey.

Do not restrict vape flavours, We want the Government to not give Ministers powers to restrict vape flavours in the Tobacco & Vapes Bill, as we believe it will undermine efforts to help smokers quit., Some studies show flavoured vapes can help people stop smoking, and we think limiting options risks pushing users back to cigarettes or other products, endangering public health.
 
We believe flavoured vaping products already play a crucial role in helping smokers quit smoking cigarettes. We believe that restricting flavours would bring more harm, reversing smoking cessation progress and pushing users to dangerous black-market products.

Create a national welfare team to oversee kennels holding seized dogs, We want the Government to create an independent national welfare team to monitor kennels used by police forces. This should include checking that staff are trained to meet the welfare standards in the Animal Welfare Act 2006 and reporting those who fail to meet those standards for prosecution., We are concerned the XL Bully Ban has massively increased seizures under DDA. We believe that many seized animals are not having their needs met, and are in some cases being returned to owners in ill health. There are reports that some seized dogs have died in kennels. We think the vast majority of seized dogs have done nothing wrong. Instead they are seized based on looks and could be held for weeks or months before assessment. We are concerned that many seized dogs may not be a banned type and could experience trauma for nothing.

End the mandate for students aged 16-18 to resit GCSE Maths and English, I urge the Department of Education/UK Government to end the mandate for GCSE resits for students aged 16-18., We feel that this system burdens our young people. Over the past few years, there has been increases in students resitting their English and Maths exams, we feel this is indicative of an outdated education system. If the DfE continues mandating resits, we fear that the mental health issues these students face will be severe. Education should prepare students, not crush their spirits and dampen their aspirations.

Create a compensation scheme for businesses affected by rail strikes, We would like the government to do something concrete to stop rail strikes. They could create a compensation scheme for the businesses effected by strikes funded by the train companies and unions., We think that the strikes can have an adverse effect on the economy of communities serviced by lines subject to regular strikes and they cannot be left until franchise renewal. The business communities do not wish for the travel disruption to continue into the summer months and beyond, whilst they are still trying to recover from COVID 19.

Stop Stubbington study centre from closing, Stubbington Study Centre is a Children’s Services facility available to schools and other pre-booked groups for residentials and more.  They want to change it to a specialist secure welfare home for 18 children., Closing Stubbington to the amount of chidren that use this site would be detrimental to future children's learning. 
For a lot of children this maybe the only chance they get to have a holiday and the only chance they get to stay away from home without parents. 
Over 6000 children a year stay at Stubbington. They are proposing to close this site and turning it in to a welfare home for only 18 children. 
The centre has been running for 90 years. Offering so much to Hampshire schools.

Reform the processes of arranging a funeral / collecting ashes, I think that, as well as the green form, an additional step should be added to the process of requesting a cremation, collecting ashes and arranging a funeral. This should be to prove that the person arranging the funeral or collecting the ashes is the next of kin or executor of the will., I don't think that the green form and death certificate should be sufficient proof to confirm someone has the right to collect ashes or organise a funeral. This will prevent families being caused distress by not being able to rightfully collect and bury ashes of a loved one.

Decrease the speed limit on country roads for the protection of animals, Decrease the speed limit on country roads to reduce the number of animals killed by cars, which could also reduce the number of accidents. This could also help the conservation of rare species that are frequently killed by vehicles, such as muntjacs and red squirrels., We think there are too many native species that are being killed due to the changing environment around roads and highways. We are concerned that that fast drivers could endanger certain species. We think slowing down vehicles would give animals/drivers more time to react and also reduce the amount of dangerous crashes caused by people driving fast on small roads.

Require all social media companies to allow infinite scrolling to be turned off, We think the Government should require all social media companies currently providing services in the UK to provide users with a means of deactivating so called ‘infinite scrolling’., Limitless scrolling is designed to ensure that social media users maintain their use for as long as possible.
We think there are many issues with this form of social media design including:
-Mental health issues
-Users losing productivity and track of time
- Decreases in attention span
- Physical health problems (poor posture and eye issues)
- Ethical issues including exploitation of users and influence of opinion by algorithms.
 
We think by allowing users to turn these functions off, users gain the control.

Bring back the Death Penalty for murder, The government should Bring back the penalty of death by execution for murder, The death Penalty is a sure and positive approach to helping stop individuals from murdering other human beings

Require recycling facilities for blister packs in all dispensaries and chemists, I want the government to reduce the amount of blister packs going into landfill by making it possible for people to recycle their medication packaging at the outlet which dispenses it., I think that by far the greatest demand for recycling is for medical blister packs. Older members of the community cannot travel to big outlets to recycle and I think the take up for recycling would be greater if we could recycle at the point of dispensing.

Lower speed limits in the uk to secure better safety for horses and riders, Lower speed limits in the uk lanes and roads to secure better safety for horses and riders, There are more distraught cases each time of riders suffering terrible injuries and horses being fatally killed and animals knocked over in the forest. The road is meant to be designed as a safe place to drive especially for young drivers and people drive far too fast is injuring or killing and animal going to get you to your destination quicker. Something needs to change for the safety of everyone thank you

Hold a referendum on the death penalty, Hold a referendum on whether the death penalty should be introduced for child killers where there is unquestionable evidence.
They did it.,

Bring back the death penalty to the UK for terrorists, murderers & paedophiles., Bring back the death penalty. The death penalty should be an option for child killers, convicted terrorists, mass murderers, serial rapists and paedophiles  Only one appeal should be allowed which must be lodged and heard within 6 months of conviction., The recent issues in the UK with child killers grooming gangs, knives crime also terrorism. Reintroducing the death sentence is crucial in our society in our opinion, this in order to set an example and teach the populace that such heinous crimes are not tolerated in the United Kingdom. As a lot of people are disrespecting the law and the authorities.

Bring back death penalty for child murderers and child sex offenders, Death penalty for people who kill children 
Death penalty for people who abuse children,

Fund access to Lecanemab on the NHS, Fund access to Lecanemab on the NHS, which is available privately for those in the early stages of Alzheimer’s but is not available on the NHS due to cost. , This drug has been shown to have significant success in reducing the progression of Alzheimer’s, a condition which can lead to the deaths of so many loved people every year. I think it's barbaric that this isn't available on the NHS due to cost, when we pay NI in our wages every month and expect treatment when needed. It is heartbreaking to see people suffer from this condition, knowing there’s a treatment that could slow the progression, and this decision and loss boils down to finances.

Drivers arrested for drug driving to be banned immediately, Change the law surrounding dangerous driving to mandate that people who are arrested for having illegal drugs in their system while driving are immediately banned, there and then. We believe this will help prevent further accidents or death.,

Make it legal responsibility for homeowners to maintain property exteriors, We think properties in disrepair due to lack of maintenance negatively devalues maintained neighbouring properties. We think the Government should enforce property standards for those lived in by owners. , We believe living next door or in the vicinity of a property in disrepair unfairly devalues neighbouring homes. Furthermore, we think it's arguable if living standards in the area are reduced it may increase the likelihood of anti-social behaviour and crime, whilst negatively impacting mental health. We think it is ultimately costing society.

Mandate life with minimum 40-year tariff for murder if the body is dismembered, We call on the Government to change the law to mandate a life sentence with a minimum tariff of 40 years in murder cases where a body has been dismembered. ,

Change the law to allow 17 year olds to purchase alcohol in a pub, Change the law so that 17 year olds can purchase alcohol in a pub under supervision of the landlord/lady. I believe this could prevent unsafe underage drinking and boost our pubs, which I think are in decline., At 17, young people are able to do many things legally e.g. drive and have children but they cannot buy alcohol to drink in a pub legally. I find this absurd. and I think it may lead 17 year olds to find alternatives ways to drink which may put them at risk or isolate them from friends in the same year, who are 18. I also believe it does not take factors such as emotional maturity to account.

Require financial service providers to issue updates about service disruptions, I want the government to introduce a law that requires banks and financial institutions to provide detailed regular updates on service disruptions and outages they are experiencing., I want the law to require them to tell us what is happening and steps they are taking to fixing it in regular intervals.

Regular updates could help give customers reassurance that they are actually doing things to fix the outage. An estimated timeline of resolution would be useful.

Review enforcement of law around vehicle transporter licenses , We want the Government to review the enforcement of rules for vehicle transporters and trailers, ensuring compliance with insurance, tax, O Licence, and tachograph regulations, creating fair competition, improving enforcement, and preventing illegal operators from undercutting legitimate businesses., Illegal vehicle transporters operate without proper insurance, O Licences, tax, or tachographs, unfairly undercutting legal businesses that follow regulations. This creates unsafe conditions and financial strain on compliant operators. We think government should review how rules are enforced to ensure only legally compliant transporters operate, improving road safety and fair competition. We urge the Government to act to protect legitimate businesses and uphold industry standards.

Require care homes to have a 1 to 5 staff to resident ratio, We are asking the government to require minimum safe staffing levels in care homes. We think there should be 1 carer for every 5 residents as otherwise care homes may not be able to provide person centred care meeting the needs of residents, We believe some care homes are understaffed and residents needs are not being met in a timely manner. We think some business owners are allowing unsafe practices due to the cost of recruiting more staff and we think this may be putting residents' safety and staff reputations at risk.

Require schools to teach about organised crime & increase police funding , Organised crime in the UK fuels drug trade, fraud, and human trafficking, harming communities and the economy. We believe the Government must boost law enforcement through increased funding and require schools to teach pupils about organised crime risks and impacts. , Crime in the UK costs billions and endangers lives through fraud and drug smuggling. We believe these dangers are not taught in schools and put young people at risk. We believe reducing UK crime and keeping communities safe can be done by boosting law enforcement and education. There are many criminals in UK networks, and we think more must be done about it urgently. We think current actions are not sufficient for public safety and we must take organised crime seriously.

Ban the sale of secondhand and unroadworthy cars to underage drivers, Make it a legal requirement at the point of sale of a secondhand vehicle to request proof of age and photo id, update the current V5C, and develop a seller portal via the DVLA vehicle check system. Failure to follow this process should lead to a prosecution or a fixed penalty for the seller, Due to the current lack of legislation with private secondhand car sales, we lost our 18 year old son to an underaged driver who was able to purchase a dangerous and unroadworthy car for £100 off a social media platform. No legal responsibility for this situation was ever placed on the seller for this tragic event. We have read about many other similar or almost identical situations. We think the government must act urgently to prevent more unnecessary tragedy

Require all to have GB licence to drive here & fund more enforcement., Require all foreign nationals to sit driving tests in Britain to drive here, to help ensure everyone is driving safely and following the rules. Fund more enforcement to check this, and to check that people aren't using fake licences.,

Justice for ESN Survivors: apologise and fund financial compensation, In the 1960s, hundreds of black children were labelled as "educationally subnormal" and wrongly sent to schools for pupils who were deemed to have low intelligence. We want the government to apologise to those affected., Many of us are suffering from lifelong trauma. Our lives are scarred by physical, mental, racial and emotional abuse. We would like closure so we can move on with our lives and get financial compensation. We think this would help us now because many of us have lost opportunities due to a lack of education in these schools for subnormal children. We feel we are outcasts in British society even though we were born in the UK.

Form a centralised microchip & DNA database for dog breeding, care, and welfare , We believe that the practices of both licensed and unlicensed breeders have resulted in many dogs and puppies suffering from serious health and welfare issues. , We consider a centralised microchip and DNA database essential to raising breeding standards, identifying and tracking hereditary diseases, and ensuring better care and welfare for all dogs.  
 
Public support has emerged for "Maggie's Law," which calls for the creation of such a database. Without mandatory tracking, DNA testing, and health checks, hereditary conditions and psychological distress in dogs are likely to continue. We believe the increasing levels of unregulated breeding highlight the urgent need for this database to support enforcement, strengthen legislation, and promote responsible ownership and welfare for breeding dogs, regardless of their licensing status.

Introduce minimum hours of driving lessons before practical driving test, The Government should review the issuing of driving licenses and introduce a legal requirement for all learner drivers to complete a minimum number of professional driving lesson hours before being allowed to take the practical driving test., I believe this could help ensure that all new drivers gain sufficient experience and skills under the supervision of a qualified instructor, helping improve road safety and potentially reducing accidents caused by inexperienced drivers.
 
Additionally, I believe this requirement could help decrease the current backlog and reduce driving test waiting times by ensuring that only well-prepared candidates book tests, leading to fewer failed attempts and a more efficient testing system.

Give students a legal right to access school toilets when they have their period, Young people who have periods during school hours are sometimes denied access to toilets. We feel that this prevents young people from having a period with dignity, causing shame. We propose young people with periods, by law be given a right to access school toilets., We believe this is inconsistent with the right to dignity and basic human rights - as per the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.

Fund more staff training and better facilities in psychiatric hospitals, We want the government to increase funding to hire and train qualified professionals who understand mental health and their side effects and can deal with difficult situations in the correct manner., Having witnessed first hand the poor treatment and neglect of mental health patients, I urge the government to increase funding for mental health services. This could ensure proper facilities in mental health units, including better bed and shower facilities. Additionally, I think patients should have access to more activities that keep them engaged and stimulated, rather than being told to stay in their rooms and sleep when they are unable to.

Reform Money Claim Court paper process and waive some fees , Greater regulations/protection in Money Claim Court applications. Require court officials be responsible for service of all claims forms/packs & conducting address checks before service to ensure respondent resides at address of service. Also for domestic abuse victims to be waived fees in disputes, Currently applicants can serve claims packs themselves, so they may deliberately omit paperwork which notifies the defendants of the need to respond to the claim. Failures to respond may result in findings against them and entries upon their credit file. We think this is being abused and can leave the defendant having to pay for the claim to be reheard. Also require court staff to conduct validity of an address for claimant/defendant to ensure they reside & are aware of cases.

Hold newspaper editors legally responsible for dangerous inaccuracies published, Introduce legal penalties specifically for newspaper editors for publishing inaccurate information that places the public or democratic process at risk., Currently we think only personal libel carries any kind of deterrent for media bodies and there isn't sufficient penalties for disinformation. We think that with increasing attacks on democracy worldwide and influence of bad faith foreign interests in the UK press it is in the interests of national security and individual safety to hold the press accountable for accuracy in a way that will actually have an impact on editorial choices.

Tax Relief for Blue Light Workers , Introduce a tax relief for Blue Light workers taking on extra shifts or working second jobs to ensure fair compensation. I think that high tax rates reduce earnings and discourage extra work., Due to high tax rates on additional income, I think our earnings are significantly reduced, leaving us inadvertently financially penalised for working extra hours. I believe this discourages essential workers from taking on vital shifts, particularly at a time when our critical public services are under immense pressure. Tax relief could provide fair compensation for our hard work and dedication.

Increase accessibility to sports facilities and promote healthy lifestyles, Build more sports facilities e.g. football pitches 
Decrease the prices to access these facilities
Promote leading healthy lifestyles e.g. eating healthy and exercise, Government has the most power and influence across the UK. This means that change at a local level can be done more efficiently.

Enforce fair compensation for short-formed train services, We want the Government to hold train operators accountable when services run with fewer carriages than scheduled. Overcrowding can make these trains unboardable, causing delays, yet there’s no clear compensation. We urge action to close this loophole and ensure fair redress for affected passengers., We feel that the current system fails to address disruption caused by short-formed services. When trains arrive with fewer carriages than scheduled, overcrowding can make them unboardable, leaving passengers stranded and late, especially if services are irregular. We feel this is more disruptive than delays and lacks a clear compensation path. We want the Government to ensure train operators are held accountable and create a fair compensation system to protect commuters from these recurring issues.

Mandate major tv broadcasters to play the national anthem at the end of the day, I think that the Tv Outlets should be required play the national anthem of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland at the end of the day like they used to., This would be mandatory for all Major Channels. I believe patriotism is important and that His Majesty deserves it

The government should make it the law for all major TV Channels to play the national anthem and portray an image of HM King Charles III at the end of the day. I think this would strengthen support for the monarchy and increase patriotism in this country as HM The King is gods representative and has a divine right to rule. I believe this is important and should be made compulsory for most channels.

Improve the National Speed Limit (NSL) road sign, Update the NSL sign to provide an indicator as to whether the road is a single or dual carriageway. The sign could be updated, for example, to include either the word 'single' or 'dual' to give further information to the driver, It is my experience, both personally and on speaking with other people, that the distinction between what constitutes a single or dual carriageway is not always clear. This may result in drivers unwittingly exceeding the speed limit which may lead to fines, injury or loss of life. Many other countries outside the UK have signs specifically indicating whether the road is a single or dual carriageway. I believe this will be beneficial to both UK and overseas drivers using UK roads.

Closing down care homes after abuse is found 
Keep service users and staff safe, More checks 
More rules and legislation 
Better safeguarding laws 
Speaking to families and staff who identify abuse 
Welfare checks 
Checking documentation 
Speak to service users directly 
Tier system, To many abuse , neglect is coming out and it’s getting worse 
All we seem to get told is that we have lessons we need to learn and not actually fixing the problem!!!

Pay compensation to families of wronged Sub-Postmasters/mistresses , We believe that those families affected by this situation should be compensated and offered help and support., This is needed because we believe that the Government is responsible for the dreadful way that the Post Office dealt with this situation, and the continuing delays that still exist after so many years.

Revoke the Mutilations (Permitted Procedures) (England) Regulations, Revoke the Mutilations (Permitted Procedures) (England) Regulations 2007 so that there are no exemptions to the prohibited procedures laid out in the Animal Welfare Act 2006., We urge the UK Government to take decisive action to end these practices and to set a new, higher standard for animal welfare that respects the sentience and dignity of all farmed animals in our country. By improving housing, enriching environments, and humane handling protocols, agriculture can be transformed into a system that prioritizes animal well-being and ethical food production. We think this could help restore public confidence and ensure that the UK leads by example.

Fund free train travel for seniors, National train fares are expensive, and even with a 1/3 discount, I think many seniors can’t afford to travel. They must pay £35 annually for a railcard just to save on tickets. This could mean missed family moments and lost independence. I feel that free travel could give them true freedom., As people get older, staying connected with family and friends becomes even more important. Yet I find that high train fares make long-distance travel impossible for many. Free national rail travel could give seniors the freedom to see loved ones, explore, and stay active while also boosting tourism and local businesses.

Require cyclists to abide by same speed limits as motor vehicles, We want the Government to legislate to change the highway code so cyclists have to abide by the speed limits on roads., Currently The Highway Code (Rule 124) and the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 don't include cyclists in speed limit regulations meant for motor vehicles. We feel this is causing a danger as it allowing cyclists to undertake vehicles which can lead to accidents. We also think it is a danger to pedestrians, a cyclist hitting a pedestrian still causes damage to both pedestrians and rider.

Hold Gig Economy Delivery companies accountable for ensuring legal road use, We urge Parliament to make it a legal duty for food delivery platforms to make sure riders are not using illegal e-bikes, riding on pavements, and ignoring traffic laws. Companies must verify compliance, share rider data with police, and face penalties for failing to act., We believe some gig economy delivery riders could be using illegally modified e-bikes that exceed legal speed limits, potentially endangering pedestrians and road users. Beyond this, some could be breaking traffic laws—riding on pavements, ignoring red lights, using one-way streets illegally, & cycling in pedestrian-only areas. We think Parliament should act to hold delivery platforms accountable & ensure compliance with UK laws.

Impose retaliatory tariffs on US goods, We believe the Government should follow suit with other countries and impose retaliatory tariffs on the US. , We believe the Government must stand up for UK businesses and jobs, and follow other countries in imposing retaliatory tariffs rather than just accepting them.

Exempt all registered motorcycles from paying Vehicle Excise Duty, We urge the Government to exempt all registered motorcycles from paying the Vehicle Excise Duty (VED). We believe accidents are being caused by the state of the roads, including delamination of the road surface but motorcycles don't have the weight to severely damage the roads., Around 350 riders on died from motorcycle accidents in 2022. We believe an increasing number of incidents may be linked to poor road surfaces. In 2021, it was estimated there were around 1.4 million motorcycle users on the road in the UK. We believe this is a very small % of the total volume of traffic who must pay VED for road surfaces they are unlikely to have damaged! We believe this is unjust and a lack of consideration by the Government for the UK’s motorcycling community.

Introduce a nationwide Baby Box scheme, We would like the government to introduce a nationwide Baby Box scheme - like that which runs in Scotland - to provide parents with a baby's first bed and essential supplies. We think this would help families give their children a safe and supported start in life., Despite Scotland successfully implementing a universal Baby Box programme since 2017, the rest of the UK has yet to follow suit. The cost of living continues to put pressure on families, and we think this would be a simple, cost-effective intervention.
 
Designed to offer a secure alternative to unsafe sleep environments, they can be packed with essential supplies. In areas where Baby Box schemes are already in place in the UK, they have been considered a lifeline for families.
Amend Law to Permit Cockerels on Allotments, Allow allotment owners/renters to have rights to own a cockerel on that land,

Require companies to pay domiciliary care workers for on-call night shifts, We urge the Government to require companies to pay domiciliary care workers fair wages for on-call night shifts, similar to on-call firefighters. We think this change would recognise their essential role and ensure they are compensated for being available to respond to emergencies., Domiciliary care workers provide life-saving care, yet they are not paid for on-call night shifts unless actively working. Meanwhile, on-call firefighters receive compensation for their availability. We think this disparity is unfair and exploitative. We think care workers face exhaustion and financial strain while ensuring vulnerable individuals receive essential overnight care. We think fair pay will improve retention, quality of care, and dignity for both workers and those they support.

Not allow Roebuck House, Cosham as temp accommodation for illegal immigrants, Cosham residents don't want Roebuck House, Cosham, Portsmouth to be temporary accommodation for illegal immigrants.
Cosham is home to many families, young, old and vulnerable and the last thing we want is to feel unsafe where we live and see a spike in crime rates like there has been around the UK, Cosham residents have a right to feel safe where they live and not feel threatened or scared about leaving their home, letting their children play, elderly relatives safety or fear that their property may be damaged or stolen. 
You only have to look at the incidents that have happened across the UK due to these temporary living arrangements to understand everyone's concerns. We would all appreciate this matter being taken seriously.

Repeal the Online Safety Act, We want the Government to repeal the Online Safety act. , We believe that the scope of the Online Safety act is far broader and restrictive than is necessary in a free society.
For instance, the definitions in Part 2 covers online hobby forums, which we think do not have the resource to comply with the act and so are shutting down instead.
We think that Parliament should repeal the act and work towards producing proportionate legislation rather than risking clamping down on civil society talking about trains, football, video games or even hamsters because it can't deal with individual bad faith actors.

Pedestrianise The Strand outside King’s College London to protect students., Following several road accidents where students have been injured or killed, most recently on Tuesday 18th March 2025, we are asking for action to be taken to fully pedestrianise The Strand by King’s College London Strand campus., There have been no measures taken to ensure students’ and the public’s safety along The Strand despite several accidents over the years. There is no through road in that direction, so there is little need for vehicles to drive through there anyway. Additionally, that area is surrounded by seating areas and benches where students study/socialise, as well as heavy tourism. We should not feel unsafe because of reckless drivers and government/university inaction to protect us.

Require All Local Authorities To Ensure That All Taxi Ranks Are Accessible, I want the Government to require all local authorities to make sure all taxi ranks have a raised area to allow wheelchair users and those with limited mobility to have easier and safer access to taxis., Many wheelchairs users might be refused taxis due to access issues, such as the taxi ramp is too steep, or the driver has an exemption to allow them to refuse to push the wheelchair user up a ramp.

Other drivers might refuse to take wheelchair users due to the time it takes to load and secure the user safely in their taxi.

By installing raised taxi ramps, we think this issue would largely be solved & more wheelchair users would be able to access public transport

The Road Traffic Act 1988, to include stopping for cats., I would like the Government to include stopping for a cat if you hit one whilst driving, leaving someone’s loved pet to die on the side of the road is cruel and should be deemed as an unlawful act., On the 25th March 2025 my beloved cat Eddie was hit by a road user and left to died on the side of the road, the driver didn’t stop to recover Eddie or even to call me; my number was on his collar along with my address. I feel this should be reviewed on The Road Traffic Act 1988 to give Cats the dignity and respect they deserve.

Require cyclists to pay road tax, We believe that given spending from the central and local government on new cycle lanes and improvements that directly benefit cyclists, the Government should require cyclists to pay road tax., Cyclists do not pay road tax to maintain our roads, and we believe that given the impoverished state of the public finances, the time has come for them to pay road tax. We believe this will ensure fairness to all road users and that everyone pays to maintain our roads.

Create a tax on clothing that contains micro-plastics, To aid in combatting the issues of plastic pollution and fast fashion, we urge the Government to implement a tax on clothing containing microplastics. With this, we aim to encourage clothing companies and brands to stop partaking in fast fashion and promote sustainability., We believe a tax on clothing with microplastics could have significant environmental benefits. Each year, large quantities of microfibers enter the ocean from washing clothes. With the UK leading Europe in clothing consumption per person, we believe urgent action is needed. We believe a tax can encourage sustainable production, reduce pollution, and drive innovation in eco-friendly materials, helping to protect marine ecosystems and promote responsible fashion practices.

Prohibit cyclists on roads with speed limits over 30mph for public safety, We want the Government to prohibit cyclists on roads with speed limits over 30mph (except organised events) for Public Safety. We think that by restricting cycling on high-speed roads and encouraging alternative infrastructure, we can reduce accidents, improve traffic efficiency, and protect lives., Many of these roads lack dedicated cycling infrastructure, which we believe can create hazards for both cyclists and motorists. We call for a ban on cyclists using roads over 30mph, except for authorised events, to reduce accidents caused by speed differences. We think this could:

- Improve traffic flow and prevent dangerous overtaking 
- Encourage better cycling infrastructure 
- Enhance safety for all road users.

We believe that this is not anti-cycling but a necessary measure to save lives.

Remove speed limits on motorways, Remove motorway speed limits, like Germany’s has autobahns.
We think people speed as they don't get to experience and enjoy high speed thrills, taking their cars into Europe, particularly the German autobahn to experience it, Although some Germans are trained to do high speed, we think it's the experience that a lot don't get to enjoy. Bring the UK in line with Europe. English version of German 'autobahn'.

Require broadband providers to offer symmetrical upload and download speeds, Set out a policy where broadband providers and Internet Service Provider's are required to offer identical upload to downloads speeds, With the rise of remote working, cloud-based applications, and content creation, we think upload speeds are just as crucial as download speeds.
As digital infrastructure is crucial for the UK’s economic growth, we think ensuring fair and future-proof broadband speeds should be a priority.

Cancel disposable vape ban, mandate plain packaging & allow 18+ to purchase, Cancel the ban on disposable vapes, and continue to allow 18+ to purchase. Stop the ban so people 18+ can continue to purchase, and to reduce the appeal to younger individuals have plain packaging like cigarettes. We feel they should not be banned for those who want to use them and are 18 plus., We believe smoking disposable e-cigarettes is a cheaper and healthier alternative than smoking and that reusable vapes do not have the same properties as disposables. We feel there are individuals who rely on disposable vapes to aid in their smoking cessation journey and who use them as a coping mechanism rather than alternatives. Some individuals may also not be able to have reusable vapes due to the high price bracket or for other reasons. We think the flavour is different too.

Require local authorities to fast track Blue Badges for seriously ill children, Require local authorities to fast track the application process for Blue Badges for children diagnosed with cancer and other serious illnesses. Consider allowing medical professionals to confirm eligibility so that families could receive temporary or emergency badges without delays., We believe delays in getting a Blue Badge application approved is leaving families with seriously ill children struggling to access hospital care and parking. In our view, this is not just an admin issue, it directly impacts quality of life & dignity of seriously ill children & their families. A fast track system would offer immediate, practical support when its is most needed.

Increase funding and strengthen penalties to stop EV charging point vandalism, We are calling on the Government to increase funding to:
-  Help the police investigate and hold criminals accountable, strengthening penalties for those caught vandalising.
- Repair and replace damaged infrastructure more quickly (units can be out of service for months). , The UK is pushing for electric vehicle (EV) adoption, but a rising problem is threatening this progress— increased vandalism of EV charging points. Across the country, charging cables are being cut, stolen, or vandalised, leaving EV owners stranded and discouraging others from making the switch. We feel the Government have done little to tackle the issue, which we think allows criminals to act with impunity. EV owners are left stranded when they cannot charge their vehicles.

Overly using Kent M20 Operation Brock contraflow!, Stop the unnecessary over use of operation Brock on the M20. It cost money every time it’s put in place
It’s dangerous for motorists and will cause a major accident on day
Traffic build up around Ashford
Using A20 has caused road damage with the increased flow of traffic
Stress and annoyance, When Brock is put into place between Maidstone & Ashford, it causes increased traffic around Ashford, especially when an accident occurs.
The local people are in uproar when Brock is implemented, it causes more issues to the roads London bound & A20 from Maidstone, whereas the traffic m20 coastal just sees an odd lorry travelling on it making it a waste of time & money. 
The cost is £250,000 at each deployment. 
Brock is most efficient when France strikes, not during school holidays!

Allow mobile use solely for real-time traffic updates when vehicles are stopped, Review and update vehicle phone laws: allow mobile access while stopped in traffic for updates and emergencies. Promote clear guidelines and support tech innovations for safer roads., We seek updated legislation because we think current laws do not reflect today’s technology. We think allowing drivers to access real-time traffic updates and emergency info while stopped could reduce congestion and prevent accidents.  We think this change supports innovation and ensures drivers stay informed, ultimately enhancing overall road safety.
Ban Drop-off charges at airports, We think it does not make any sense to ask passengers to pay when they are dropping-off their loved ones., We think drop-off charges at airports should be banned.

Require Give Way signs to be positioned on major slip roads, Require local councils to place a Give Way sign at all major slip roads. I believe the amount of near misses and accidents at slip roads supplying carriage ways and motor ways can be greatly reduced by placing Give Way signs. , I think a number of motorists are unaware of the need to give way to traffic moving at speed when transferring from slip road to main road and a simple sign will educate motorists.

Make mass littering and disturbances in a cinema a fineable crime, We think we need to hold people responsible for creating disturbances and littering in cinemas. We think these activities should be illegal and punished with fines., Not only does littering mean that some cleaners have to stay back for hours to clean, but disturbances mean that some people who have paid to watch the movie cannot focus or concentrate. Small children could be left in tears and fear in a dark cinema room with shouting and disturbances.

Introduce increased regulation of letting agents, We call on the Government to introduce increased regulation for letting agents by establishing an independent regulator with enforcement powers, a mandatory licensing scheme, recognised qualifications for letting agents, and transparent fees and conduct standards., Letting agents currently operate without formal oversight, and we think this has led to hidden fees, withheld deposits, potentially misleading advertising, and pressure tactics. We think tenants can be exploited, and landlords may be unfairly blamed for poor agent conduct. We believe this lack of accountability damages trust in the housing market and leaves the public vulnerable.
 
Housing is essential and we believe letting agents must be held to professional standards.

Require reptile shops to ensure higher standards in reptile care and equipment, We believe that without basic set ups - as recommended by animal welfare experts - in terms of lighting and vivaria size, it can be detrimental to a bearded dragon's health and cause metabolic bone disease among other serious health conditions. There needs to be a change. , We think that reptile shops and pet shops can sell bearded dragons to purchasers without adequate lighting or husbandry, and may also be selling the incorrect lighting and husbandry themselves. The government should require shops to prove a customer has an adequate set up before allowing a purchase of a bearded dragon, and should require shops to only stock equipment which ensures a suitable environment for the animal, in accordance with the principles set out in the Animal Welfare Act 2006.

Introduce a national licensing scheme for commercial dog walking, Commercial dog walkers do not currently require a licence in most areas, and can operate unchecked with no regulation. I believe a national licence would ensure the safety and well-being of both dogs and the public., Walking dogs requires knowledge of dog behaviour, first aid, transport laws, and responsible handling. I believe a licence would establish minimum standards that dog walkers must meet. Currently, walkers may take more dogs than they can handle, which could be unsafe. I believe a licence would regulate numbers. If a licensed walker acts irresponsibly, their licence could be suspended/revoked and this could give incentive to follow conditions.

Make it easier to obtain a licence to produce/grow medical cannabis, We feel that it is currently extremely difficult to apply for a controlled drugs licence to grow cannabis high in THC for medical use in the UK. , We think the US have a more friendly licensing application for the public to enter the medical cannabis market and that in the UK it is much harder to obtain a licence. We believe that allowing more people to produce medical cannabis in the UK could create thousands of jobs across the country and could boost the economy massively.

Introduce tax relief on Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) , Introduce tax relief on RSUs. We think the tax structure on RSUs is unfair & may harm UK startups competing for talent. We think a tax relief would ensure fairer tax on unrealised value, help startups grow, boost UK innovation & economy, creating jobs & future tax revenue.,

Require supermarkets to offer nutrition-based filtering and alerts online, We want the government to require online supermarkets to display real-time nutrition tracking (e.g. salt, sugar) as you shop, allow filtering for dietary needs (like diabetic or gluten-free), warn users when thresholds are exceeded and remove junk food ads for users with dietary preferences., There are limits on how much medicine you can buy online, yet no checks on food. We think that supermarkets already have the data and tech—they just need to join it up. We are concerned people are unknowingly adding harmful amounts to their baskets. We think it's a simple change that could improve public health.
 
It could help the obesity crisis, hospital admissions and make people more well-informed and ultimately give some accountability to the supermarkets who we think are part of the problem.

Ban insured deposit protection schemes, Please amend the law to provide greater protections to tenants by banning insured deposit protection schemes., Currently, landlords must register tenant's deposits within 30 days and provide prescribed information.
 
There are two types of TDP schemes: (1) Insured and (2) Custodial Scheme.
 
The insured scheme allows the landlord/agent to keep control of the deposit for a fee.
 
We think there aren't adequate safeguards for tenants under this arrangement.
Tenants may have to go to court to get their deposit back - spending time and more money. Even with a court order against the landlord, the tenant may have to apply for enforcement if the landlord does not follow the order from the Court.

Remove the ‘right to roam’ status applicable to domesticated cats, We feel it is now time to end the 'right to roam' for cats. Cats can have a serious impact on wildlife. A study published in 2022 estimated that cats kill 160 to 270 million animals every year, 25% of them are birds., Secondly, cats can leave droppings in private gardens which can cause series illnesses such as toxoplasmosis. Thirdly, cats can destroy flower beds, lawns and pots. Finally, cats themselves are at risk. Every day in the UK 630 cats are killed in road traffic accidents. Some families have no idea what has happened to their beloved pet.

Introduce measures to ensure fair pay for rideshare drivers, Some firms can charge drivers commission fees of 25% or more of each fare. This can leave drivers struggling to earn a fair and sustainable income. We think this model places an unfair burden on drivers, who are essential to our transport infrastructure but we feel lack basic rights and protections., 1. Introduce legislation to cap the commission fees that rideshare companies can take from drivers.
2. Support the creation and growth of a UK-based, more driver-friendly rideshare company that operates with fairer practices, more transparency, and better driver welfare.
3. Strengthen regulatory oversight of the gig economy.
 
Drivers deserve dignity, respect, and the right to earn a fair living. Let’s take a stand for fairness and support homegrown innovation in the UK transport sector.

Change the speed limit for single-carriageway rural roads from 60mph to 30mph, Rural roads are the most dangerous roads for all kinds of driver and speed is the problem. A study of single-carriageway rural roads estimated that a 10% increase in average speed results in a 30% increase in fatal and serious crashes. , I think the fact that drivers can legally do 60mph is absolute negligence and shows a disregard for human life. Rural roads account for well over half of all fatal crashes. Cyclists, motorcyclists and car drivers are more than three times as likely to be killed per mile travelled on a rural road than an urban road.
 
Even if you are driving slowly, others may not be. I think this change is urgent.

Install CCTV along York Riversides, Cycle paths and Children’s Play parks., CCTV cameras installed down both sides of the rivers running through York, and additional CCTV installed down old train lines which are now cycle paths and children’s play areas., Predatory behaviour towards all people and attacks of all varieties have been on the up in the last decade  in York, and Camera surveillance although it may not stop the problem it would provide substantial deterrence and evidence of crimes that do still happen.

Require vets to check cats and dogs recorded microchip details yearly, We want the Government to amend The Microchipping of Cats and Dogs (England) Regulations 2023 to require vets to scan pets’ microchips yearly (i.e. when vaccinations are due) and check the owners details against the database to ensure the chip is registered and the details are up to date., Of the many dogs collected by wardens nationally every week, we believe some are not microchipped. Of those that are, many may have either unregistered chips or ones still linked to breeders or previous owners. Some owners might not realise they need to register the chip themselves, and some might forget to update details. Vets might not check that the chips are correctly registered/up to date. We believe yearly database checking by vets could alert them to problems and help prevent issues later

Increase minimum penalties for hate crimes against transgender people, We want the government to impose harsher penalties on those who believe it's acceptable to attack someone for being transgender, including a minimum jail time of 6 months for those convicted of hate crimes against transgender people.,

Review the use of speed cameras, We would like there to be an independent review into the use of speed cameras., We want it to look into:
- Fixed locations and times for mobile units.
- Removal of financial punitive measures.
- Reassessing the points and fines structure.
 
We feel that cameras, particularly mobile speed cameras are being deployed at an alarmingly high rate.

Require companies to cap price increases to 20% during school holidays, We want the Government to make it law that holiday companies can only raise prices by a maximum of 20% during school holidays. We feel families are currently unfairly charged because they are limited to travelling in school holidays. We feel it would make access to holidays fairer., Families with school-age children are often forced to travel during school breaks and holiday companies raise prices, in our opinion by huge amounts. We think this makes holidays unaffordable for many, leaving only wealthier families able to go away. We think a 20% cap would stop such large price hikes, making sure all families have a fairer chance to enjoy a break together. We feel holidays are important for family time, rest, and creating memories, and they shouldn’t just be for those who can afford massive extra costs.

Increase engine power limit for motorcycle drivers on CBT license, Allow CBT license holders to ride motorcycles that have more than 15bhp while still maintaining the 125cc engine size. We think 25bhp should be the maximum power allowed on a CBT license for those aged 17 and older., We think that 15bhp is an unsafe amount of power for a motorcycle. We feel it can be dangerous when turning onto roads with a speed limit of more than 40mph+ as some motorcycles cannot reliably reach the speed limit in time to ensure the rider can safely enter the road. We feel that 25bhp is a more reasonable limit as it will allow the motorcycle to reach the desired speed in time and minimises the risk to the rider and other road users and is also still manageable for inexperienced motorcyclists.

Change speeding penalties to 1point for up to 25MPH on a 20MPH road, We feel that the current penalty of 3 points for speeding in 20mph areas is disproportionate. We think the current penalty treats these drivers the same as other drivers who speed at much higher limits., In areas like London, drivers can be penalised for doing 24mph in 20mph areas, which we feel is heavily punishing. We feel it's easy to collect multiple 3 points penalties if drivers are making many journeys. We would like the penalties reviewed. Penalties can impact drivers insurance costs and can affect their ability to work.

Fund access to bicycles for children so they can live active and healthy lives, We want the Government to fund access to a bicycle for every child so they can be active and more healthy., We believe this is important so children can be more active and healthy. Healthy children are less likely to go to the doctors so we think this could reduce NHS waiting times and the strain on them. Riding a bicycle is better for the environment. It may also reduce traffic around schools that could reduce the chances of accidents.
 
We think bicycles are a great way to travel because they are faster than walking and doesn't use up fuels.
Require all new trains to be fitted with seatbelts, We want the government to make it law that all new trains are fitted with seatbelts, to help prevent fatalities.,

Update school uniform guidance to prioritise comfort for students in England, We urge the Government to update guidance on school uniforms in England, so that it prioritises comfort and addresses: breathable fabrics, flexible designs, and seasonal options. We believe comfortable uniforms help students focus, feel confident, and learn better in school., We want the Government to ensure school uniforms are comfortable and inclusive for all learners, including neurodivergent students who may struggle with restrictive fabrics or seams. We think current uniforms can affect focus and wellbeing. We propose updating the guidance to allow more flexible options, like PE kit-style clothing, made from breathable materials and branded with school logos to maintain identity. We believe this could support comfort, inclusivity, and confidence, helping all students engage better in their learning.

Ban the Ring Flying disc to Protect Our Seals, Young seals sometimes find lost or discarded flying rings (any type of throwing ring). Being inquisitive, they sometimes play with them, putting their heads through the hole & may become trapped. As they grow, the rings can cut into their necks, causing life threatening open wounds & sometimes death, Seals around the UK are protected wild animals. Legislation does not allow any suffering, killing or injuring of our heritage seals. However, this may be caused by flying rings. Flying rings may be lost or discarded on beaches, and may end up in the sea. We think the use of existing solid discs, preferably biodegradable, are seal safe alternatives.
